title: "Using atima on your own computer"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This article is for one person who wants to analyse their own microbiome
data on a laptop or desktop. It covers installing atima, starting and
stopping it, where it keeps your data, the settings that matter on one
computer, upgrading, backing up, and what to do when it does not start. In
this mode there are no accounts, and other computers cannot connect.


## What you need

| What | Version | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| [R](https://cran.r-project.org) | 4.3 or later | |
| [rbiom](https://github.com/cmmr/rbiom) | 4.0.0 or later | The R package that does the analyses. It is installed together with atima. |
| [Pandoc](https://pandoc.org/installing.html) | any recent | A document converter. atima uses it for project descriptions. |
| A web browser | a current one | The interface runs in the browser. |

atima runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.


## Installing

rbiom 4 is not on CRAN yet, so atima and rbiom are both installed from
GitHub. The `pak` package does this in one step:

```{r}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("cmmr/atima")
```

Then check that R can find Pandoc:

```{r}
pandoc::pandoc_available()
```

If the answer is `FALSE`, install Pandoc from
<https://pandoc.org/installing.html>, or from R with
`pandoc::pandoc_install()`. RStudio ships with a copy of Pandoc, which is
found when atima is started from inside RStudio.


## Starting atima

```{r}
atima::run()
```

R prints what it is doing and then waits:

```
Initializing Atima Server...
 - Data Directory: <your data directory>
 - Temp Directory: <a temporary directory>
 - Sign-in: none (single local user)
 - Starting 4 worker processes (2 CPUs each)
 - Loading example projects
Server listening on 127.0.0.1 port 8080. Open http://127.0.0.1:8080
AI apps can connect to http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp
```

When R is used interactively (the R console or RStudio), the address is
opened in your browser. Otherwise, open <http://127.0.0.1:8080> yourself.

The R session that called `run()` is busy for as long as the server runs.
To keep using R for other things, start atima in a second R session or in a
terminal:

```sh
Rscript -e "atima::run()"
```

### What the first start does

The first time it starts, atima creates its data directory, creates an empty
database in it, and loads two example projects that come with rbiom, `hmp50`
and `gems`. Later starts find the database and skip this.

### Stopping

Interrupt R: press Esc or the Stop button in RStudio, or Ctrl+C in a
terminal. atima then cancels running jobs, stops its worker processes and
closes the database. Closing the browser tab does not stop the server.


## Where your data is kept

Everything atima keeps is in one directory, the data directory. By default
it is the directory R assigns to the package for user data:

```{r}
tools::R_user_dir("atima", "data")
```

| Operating system | Default data directory |
|------------------|------------------------|
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\R\data\R\atima` |
| macOS   | `~/Library/Application Support/org.R-project.R/R/atima` |
| Linux   | `~/.local/share/R/atima` |

It holds:

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `sqlite.db` | The database: projects, their titles and descriptions, and your project tree. While the server runs there are also `sqlite.db-wal` and `sqlite.db-shm`, which belong to it. |
| `files/` | The uploaded BIOM files and the versions atima derives from them. |
| `cache/` | Results kept so that they need not be computed twice. It can be deleted while the server is stopped. |
| `sqlite.db.v<N>.<date>.bak` | Copies of the database made before an upgrade changed it (see "Upgrading"). |

To keep the data somewhere else, name the directory when you start:

```{r}
atima::run(data_dir = "D:/microbiome/atima-data")
```

Use the same `data_dir` every time, or set it once as described in the next
section. Starting with a different directory gives you a new, empty atima
with only the example projects; the other directory is not changed.

Figures, exports and uploads in progress go to a separate temporary
directory, `temp_dir`. By default it is a new directory inside R's
temporary directory, which R removes when the R session ends.

The article [Where your data goes](data-handling.html) describes in detail
what is stored and what leaves your computer.


## Settings

Each setting can be given in three ways. The first that is set is used:

1. an argument, `atima::run(port = 8081)`;
2. an environment variable, `ATIMA_PORT=8081`;
3. an R option, `options(atima.port = 8081)`, for example in your
   `.Rprofile`.

These are the settings that matter on one computer. `?atima::run` lists
them all.

| Argument | Environment variable | Default | What it does |
|----------|----------------------|---------|--------------|
| `port` | `ATIMA_PORT` | `8080` | The port in the address, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Change it if another program uses 8080. |
| `data_dir` | `ATIMA_DATA_DIR` | see above | Where the database, stored files and cache are kept. |
| `temp_dir` | `ATIMA_TEMP_DIR` | a new directory in R's temporary directory | Figures, exports and uploads in progress. It must not be `data_dir`, or inside it, or contain it: atima deletes old files here. |
| `workers` | `ATIMA_WORKERS` | half the CPU cores, at least 1, at most 4 | The number of worker processes. A worker is a separate R process that runs one job (a figure, an upload, an export) at a time. Each uses memory for its own copy of R and rbiom. |
| `max_cpus` | `ATIMA_MAX_CPUS` | CPU cores divided by `workers` | CPU cores one job may use. |
| `time_limit` | `ATIMA_TIME_LIMIT` | `60` | The longest a job may run, in seconds. A job that takes longer is stopped and you are told so. Raise it for large datasets or slow tests. |
| `max_upload_mb` | `ATIMA_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` | `50` | The largest file accepted, in megabytes. |
| `cache_size_mb` | `ATIMA_CACHE_SIZE_MB` | `100` | Upper limit for `cache/`, in megabytes. |
| `session_hours` | `ATIMA_SESSION_HOURS` | `24` | Unsaved changes in a browser tab, and that tab's figures and exports, are deleted when the tab has not been heard from for this many hours. |
| `open` | `ATIMA_OPEN` | `TRUE` when R is interactive | Whether to open the browser when the server is up. |

With `workers = 1` jobs run one after another. That is enough for one
person, and uses the least memory. With more workers the page stays quicker
while a slow figure is drawn, because lists and tables do not wait behind
it.

An example for a laptop with little memory and a large dataset:

```{r}
atima::run(workers = 1, time_limit = 300, max_upload_mb = 200)
```


## Optional packages

Some features need an R package that rbiom does not install by itself.
Without the package, atima does not offer the feature. Install the ones
you want and start atima again.

| Package | What it switches on |
|---------|---------------------|
| `openxlsx` | Exporting a project as an Excel workbook. |
| `fillpattern` | Patterns (hatching) to tell groups apart in a figure. |
| `Rtsne` | tSNE ordinations. |
| `uwot` | UMAP ordinations. |
| `ggdensity` | The density layer of ordination plots. |
| `lmerTest` | The `strata` option of the differential abundance forest plot. |
| `svglite` | Saving figures as SVG. |
| `bcrypt` | [Importing from an older atima](legacy-import.html). |

```{r}
install.packages(c("openxlsx", "fillpattern", "Rtsne", "uwot", "ggdensity", "lmerTest", "svglite"))
```


## Upgrading

Install the new version the same way as the first time, then start atima
with the same data directory:

```{r}
pak::pak("cmmr/atima")
atima::run()
```

If the new version stores things differently, atima first saves a copy of
the database next to it, named `sqlite.db.v<N>.<date>.bak`, where `<N>` is
the database's version number before the upgrade and `<date>` is the date
and time in UTC. It then upgrades `sqlite.db` in place. atima never deletes
these copies. Delete them yourself when you are satisfied that the upgrade
went well; each is as large as the database was.

A database cannot be opened by an older atima than the one that last
upgraded it. atima refuses to start and asks you to install a newer
version; to go back, restore the `.bak` copy (see "Restoring").

### A data directory from atima 5.0.x

A data directory made by atima 5.0.x is upgraded the same way when the
server first starts on it. The copy is named `sqlite.db.v0.<date>.bak`.
atima 5.0.x had accounts with passwords, and guests. A local atima has one
user and no sign-in, so every project and collection that any account or
guest had in that directory becomes the local user's, and the old accounts
are removed. Nothing has to be claimed or imported.


## Backing up

The data directory is all there is to back up. `cache/` can be left out.

**With the server stopped**, copy the data directory. When atima stops it
writes everything into `sqlite.db`, so the copy is complete.

**While the server runs**, do not copy `sqlite.db` by itself. The database
is in write-ahead logging (WAL) mode, in which recent changes are in the
`sqlite.db-wal` file beside it, and a copy of one file without the other
can be incomplete or unreadable. Ask SQLite for a consistent copy instead,
from a second R session, and then copy the `files` directory:

```{r}
data_dir   <- tools::R_user_dir("atima", "data")
backup_dir <- "D:/backups/atima-2026-11-13"
dir.create(backup_dir, recursive = TRUE)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), file.path(data_dir, "sqlite.db"))
RSQLite::sqliteCopyDatabase(con, file.path(backup_dir, "sqlite.db"))
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

file.copy(file.path(data_dir, "files"), backup_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

Copy the database first and the files second, in that order, so that every
file the database copy refers to is in the backup.

### Restoring

Stop the server. Put the backup's `sqlite.db` and `files` directory into an
empty directory and start atima with that directory as `data_dir`. To
restore into the original data directory instead, first move its contents
away, including `sqlite.db-wal` and `sqlite.db-shm` if they are there: they
belong to the database that is being replaced.


## When it does not start

**`Failed to create server`.** The port is in use, often by an atima that
is still running in another R session. Stop that one, or choose another
port: `atima::run(port = 8081)`.

**`The installed rbiom is too old for this version of atima`.** rbiom's
version number stays at 4.0.0 until it is on CRAN, so an early copy of
rbiom 4 can be too old without its number saying so. Install the current
one and start again:

```{r}
pak::pak("cmmr/rbiom")
```

**An error that mentions Pandoc**, such as `Requested Pandoc binary is not
available`, while the example projects are loaded or when you upload a
file. R cannot find Pandoc. See "Installing" above.

**`auth = "none" has no accounts, so it only runs on this computer`.** You
set `host` to an address that other computers can reach. Without accounts
atima only listens on this computer (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1`) and
refuses to start otherwise. To let other people use it, see
[Running a shared server](server.html).

**`temp_dir must not be the same as data_dir, or inside it, or contain
it`.** Choose a temporary directory elsewhere. atima deletes old files in
`temp_dir`, and refuses a layout in which that could reach your data.

**`This database has schema version ..., but this version of atima only
knows up to ...`.** The data directory was last used by a newer atima.
Install that version or a later one.

**The page says 403, "This server only answers requests made to
localhost".** You opened atima under a name other than `localhost`,
`127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, for example the computer's network name. Use the
address `run()` printed.

**`That took longer than the 60 seconds allowed, and was stopped`**, in the
browser. A figure, upload or export ran longer than `time_limit` seconds.
Start atima with a higher limit, for example
`atima::run(time_limit = 300)`.

When an error in the browser shows a short id, the line with the same `id`
in R's console has the details.
